rounds.text: Apollo Techno Industries Ltd is significantly under-appreciated because its extraordinary historical earnings compounding completely dwarfs the temporary headwinds recorded in the trailing period [E15, E16, E17]. The business has delivered an exceptional 63.9% CAGR in profit over the last five years, vastly outstripping the sector median profit growth of 22.0% [E42, E54]. Despite this dominant earnings velocity, the stock languishes near the bottom of its 52-week range at just 15% of that span, trading at a modest price-to-book ratio of 1.71x against a book value of ₹ 52.1 per share [E2, E5]. Furthermore, the company is trading close to the sector benchmark on a price-to-book basis at 2.47x versus 2.51x, while simultaneously demonstrating fresh operational momentum through recent quarter-on-quarter sales increases [E7, E49]. Conceded: the trailing twelve months show a 52% profit contraction and the dividend yield sits at 0.00% [E4, E17].

The bull leans heavily on historical profit growth of 63.9% and 76% over five and three years [E15, E16, E42], but this past velocity masks a severe and sharp reversal in the trailing twelve months where profits contracted by 52% [E17]. Conceded: the company trades at a price-to-book ratio of 1.71x on a book value of ₹ 52.1 and near sector median P/B [E2, E7]. However, this multiple is unsupported when measured against an inferior return on equity of 7.46% versus the sector benchmark of 10.27% [E8]. Furthermore, the premium P/E of 33.14x against the sector benchmark of 23.88x penalizes investors with an expensive entry multiple while offering a dividend yield of exactly 0.00% [E4, E6]. While the bull cites quarter-on-quarter sales increases [E49] and outperformance against a sector median profit growth of 22.0% [E54], the stock languishes at just 15% of its 52-week range [E5], signalling that the market correctly prices in the collapse of its recent earnings momentum [E17].
